narrative.overview: Practical and organised: everything has a labelled place, controls are sturdy enough for wet hands, and nothing is there for decoration. Colour comes from the content, not the chrome.
keyCharacteristics: One lead per screen; supporting facts as quiet text and grouped rows, never a grid of equal tiles.
Flat. No drop shadows except controls floating over the map.
System font only, seven text roles, three weights (400, 600, 700). Sentence case everywhere.
Forest is the only interactive colour; lime only marks a personal highlight.

rules.name: The One Tint Rule
rules.body: Forest is the only colour that means "you can press this" or "this is selected".

rules.name: The Highlight Rule
rules.body: Lime appears only where something is personally notable (new species, PB).

rules.name: The Sun Rule
rules.body: Body and secondary text stay at or above 4.5:1 against whatever they sit on.

rules.name: The Seven Roles Rule
rules.body: Every text uses one of the seven roles, through the theme.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No shadows on cards, tiles, sections or buttons.

dos: Do give every screen one lead (photo, fish, lake, map) and keep everything else in Body/Secondary text or grouped rows.
Do write numbers as one quiet line when there are several.
Do use the theme's text roles and colours; screens should not contain raw sizes or hex values.
Do keep touch targets at least 44×44pt (48dp on Android).
Do credit data sources in a Secondary line next to the data.
donts: Don't put boxes inside boxes, or show a row of equal stat tiles.
Don't add drop shadows outside the map.
Don't use uppercase letter-spaced labels or weight 800.
Don't use lime for buttons, disabled states or ordinary panels.
Don't show a stat that is zero just to fill a tile.
Don't use web patterns: breadcrumbs, underlined links, hover hints.
